publication_copy.headline: ROOM ABOVE TWO HUNDRED
publication_copy.deck: The week the pressure reached everyone
publication_copy.body: By Sunday night, the Commonwealth had learned that a number could become a weapon without anyone lifting a blade. Two teams had crossed two hundred. One sent a hamburger to a birthday party; another brought an army to a mountain gate. A centaur was chasing an outlaw through Highland mud. In the eastern ruins, a river quietly made a mockery of Red Leopards's sandbags, while a second gust carried the same storm's reach to a court farther inland. Seven Deadly Chins found the one household that needed quiet and arrived with a jackhammer. Slob on my Dobb made a beer delivery through a swamp whose owner could no longer command the road. The front belonged to El Niño; the humiliations belonged to the men who chose them. With four regular-season games remaining after this one, the question was no longer simply who won. It was what each result would leave behind.

publication_copy.headline: KEEP THE WHOLE LEAGUE IN VIEW
publication_copy.deck: Commissioner’s note • Draft address
publication_copy.body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. Tonight's remaining starters can still move the board. When those numbers settle, the next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.
